ceiling_fan.title: Ceiling fan for HomeKit
ceiling_fan.description:
A Fanv2 plus a Lightbulb in one accessory. Pick the fan or switch entity that turns it on and off. The next step offers every entity of the same device for the other parts.

Fields also accept number, input_number and select entities. On/off uses a number's minimum and maximum, or a select's Off-style and On-style options (otherwise their order). Sliders use the numeric range or the option order.

ceiling_fan_parts.title: Ceiling fan: parts
ceiling_fan_parts.description:
Power: {power} ({count} entities on its device). Each part gets a dropdown of every entity of that device, so any of them can serve any part; numbers and selects are offered for every part. Pick 'Other entity…' to choose an entity from elsewhere on the next step. Speed is mapped onto HomeKit's percentage slider automatically. Direction: a fan's forward, a select's first option and a switch's off are clockwise; tick Reverse if the direction shown in the Home app is the opposite of what the blades do. Oscillation accepts a fan, switch, input_boolean, number, input_number or select. For numbers, minimum = off and maximum = on. For selects, Off/Disabled = off (otherwise the first option), and the first remaining option = on; other options also report on. Mode is the fan (its presets) or a select whose options give HomeKit's Auto/Manual switch (you name the two options next), or a switch (on = Auto). A temperature sensor is published as a separate temperature reading in the same accessory. Tick 'Name the speeds' to publish one extra switch per speed level, named after the select's options or the number's values, since HomeKit's own speed slider is always a percentage. Exactly one is on at a time, and switching the on one off stops the fan. A speed source with more than 12 levels cannot be named. Leave a part blank to skip it; with a fan entity as power, blank speed, direction, oscillate and mode fall back to the fan's own features. A 'Last HomeKit write' sensor on the device shows the last value the Home app sent. After saving, a notification shows the setup code.

Fields also accept number, input_number and select entities. On/off uses a number's minimum and maximum, or a select's Off-style and On-style options (otherwise their order). Sliders use the numeric range or the option order.

data.named_speeds: Name the speeds (adds a Low / Medium / High style switch per speed)
data.back: Go back to the previous step instead (the rest of this form is ignored)

ceiling_fan_mode.title: Ceiling fan: Auto mode
ceiling_fan_mode.description:
Mode entity: {mode}. It offers: {options}. Choose which one means Auto (a breeze, smart or auto mode) and which means Manual; HomeKit then shows its Auto/Manual switch. A fan entity may leave Manual empty (Manual then re-asserts the speed); a select needs both. Leave both empty for no switch.

Fields also accept number, input_number and select entities. On/off uses a number's minimum and maximum, or a select's Off-style and On-style options (otherwise their order). Sliders use the numeric range or the option order.

data.back: Go back to the previous step instead (the rest of this form is ignored)
